source.title: Opt-Out: Investigating Entity-Level Unlearning for Large Language Models via Optimal Transport
source.authors: Minseok Choi; Daniel Rim; Dohyun Lee; Jaegul Choo

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates entity-level unlearning and adversarial prompt attacks using its own metrics and dataset. It does not reproduce the specific recovery interventions in the claim.
record.gate_note: The main unlearning table reports the study's own Forget Quality (FQ), Retain Quality (RQ), and benchmark utility results. Figure 3 reports FQ under nine adversarial prompt attack types; the text explicitly says Opt-Out maintains high-quality forgetting across them, but the attack-specific plotted values are not available in the extracted text. The study does not test post-unlearning relearning, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or a mechanism that distinguishes blocked access from deleted knowledge. Cited findings from other papers are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: This is a new-method paper (Opt-Out) set in entity-level unlearning of real Wikipedia entities. Its own results bear on A: forget-set accuracy proxies drop while benchmark utility holds. They also bear on E and F: nine adversarial prompt attacks were run on Llama-3.1-8B. It runs no relearning, ablation or quantization attack.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that Opt-Out beats existing unlearning methods on entity-level forgetting while keeping retention and benchmark utility, and that it is robust to MIAs and nine prompt attacks. They also note it can still produce gibberish after unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces optimal-transport-based Wasserstein regularization with NPO and retain-set training for entity-level unlearning; it does not apply the proposed fine-tuning, activation-edit, or quantization recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differ by model: for example, Guardrail FQ is 64.8 on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and 34.9 on Phi-3.5-Mini-Instruct. Unlearning without retain-set training is reported to cause collapse.

fits_no_version.finding: MIA classifier accuracy for Opt-Out is 48.6% (Llama) and 49.1% (Phi), against a 50% oracle (Table 2). IDK+RT is at 69.1% and 67.3%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Membership-inference distinguishability after unlearning varies by method; refusal-training methods leave detectable traces.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study uses Wikipedia-derived proxy sets rather than actual user privacy data, evaluates two models below 70B parameters, and notes that gibberish can still occur after unlearning. FQ is a composite proxy rather than a direct accuracy-to-chance test. Figure 3's attack-specific values are not available in the extracted text.
record.rows_left_out: The row limit was not reached. Table 1 results for other methods' RQ and benchmark averages are omitted except where needed to show retention and collapse. Detailed metric components in Table 6, distance-metric comparisons in Table 3, and individual benchmark scores are omitted as supplementary or duplicative for these claim versions. Figure 3's separate attack-specific plotted values could not be extracted; the aggregate Opt-Out result stated in Section 4.5 is recorded in r33.

untested.parts: Robustness to fine-tuning, internal-edit and quantization attacks. 'Near chance' is only indirect: FQ is a composite, and there is no multiple-choice chance baseline.
Entirely untested: no activation ablation or access-versus-deletion analysis.
Prompt attacks were run on Llama-3.1-8B only, not Phi-3.5. Per-attack values are not readable.
Opt-Out's robustness was tested only against prompt attacks and MIAs, not relearning, ablation or quantization. Phi-3.5 was not tested under attacks.

missing.what: Forget-set Prob and ROUGE for Opt-Out, which measure knowledge removal directly. Llama: Prob 40.7→2.2, ROUGE 63.7→6.3. Phi: Prob 11.1→5.2, ROUGE 64.6→9.9.
Per-attack FQ for the +RT baselines and Opt-Out under the nine prompt attacks (figure only).
TOFU exact-unlearning comparison: Opt-Out FQ* 86.6 on both models, versus 0.0-71.3 for the +RT baselines.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new-method paper in a new entity-level setting, not an attack study. FQ is a harmonic mean of inverted Prob, ROUGE and truth ratio, not accuracy against chance. The E and F verdicts rest only on the authors' prose about Figure 3.

versions.untested_parts: Uses FQ as an unlearning proxy, not a direct accuracy-to-chance comparison. Does not test whether simple attacks fail for every unlearning method.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning attack using unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis establishing access blocking rather than deletion.
Tests nine adversarial prompt types, not every listed form of rephrasing, jailbreak, language change, or in-context recovery. Attack-specific values are not extractable from the provided figure text.
Tests Opt-Out against adversarial prompt attacks only; does not test robustness to fine-tuning, internal edits, or quantization.
